question: What is the primary characteristic of a polyvalent nurse compared to a specialized nurse?

options.A: Focus strictly on administrative duties rather than direct bedside nursing
options.B: Exclusive expertise in managing critical care and intensive care units
options.C: Possession of a broad and versatile range of multi-functional competencies
options.D: Advanced academic degrees in pharmacological research and pathology

explanation: Polyvalent nursing emphasizes cross-functional training and a wide skill set rather than narrow clinical specialization. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: How does polyvalent nursing primarily benefit healthcare delivery systems?

options.A: By completely eliminating the need for physician consultations
options.B: By bridging gaps between clinical departments through holistic care
options.C: By reducing the total duration of basic nursing education training
options.D: By restricting nurses to a single, highly predictable ward routine

explanation: Versatile nursing roles help connect fragmented services, allowing clinicians to address overall patient needs smoothly across settings. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: What does multi-skilling primarily allow a polyvalent nurse to do?

options.A: Manage hospital financial budgets and payroll systems
options.B: Transition across diverse clinical duties without compromising safety
options.C: Prescribe controlled medications without medical supervision
options.D: Perform major surgical operations independently without a surgeon

explanation: Multi-skilling equips the nurse to handle varied clinical tasks safely across different departments. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which activity best demonstrates the preventive aptitude of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on end-stage palliative care management
options.B: Conducting forensic autopsies in hospital morgue facilities
options.C: Integrating immunization tracking and health promotion into ward routines
options.D: Performing routine maintenance on biomedical laboratory equipment

explanation: Preventive competencies involve actively promoting wellness and monitoring community health alongside curative duties. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary driver for adaptability in polyvalent nursing practice?

options.A: Strict adherence to rigid, unchanging daily ward schedules
options.B: The absolute abundance of medical supplies and personnel
options.C: Elimination of all emergency admissions in the hospital
options.D: Sudden shifts in patient acuity and unpredictable healthcare demands

explanation: Adaptability is essential because healthcare environments constantly face fluctuating patient numbers and varying emergency needs. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: A nurse is reassigned from a postnatal ward to a busy accident and emergency unit due to a sudden mass casualty incident. What action best reflects polyvalent adaptability?

options.A: Rapidly recalibrating clinical priorities and applying rapid assessment frameworks
options.B: Insisting on remaining in the postnatal ward to maintain personal routine
options.C: Delegating all emergency patient assessments strictly to junior ward attendants
options.D: Refusing the redeployment until formal specialist re-certification is completed

explanation: A polyvalent nurse responds to urgent staffing needs by quickly adjusting focus and utilizing generalist crisis skills. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: What primary role does the polyvalent nurse play within the interdisciplinary team?

options.A: Acting as the sole decision-maker for all medical treatment plans
options.B: Isolating nursing care completely from other healthcare professions
options.C: Reviewing and grading the performance evaluations of attending physicians
options.D: Serving as a central communication node synthesizing clinical findings

explanation: Polyvalent nurses bridge different specialties by gathering and communicating comprehensive patient data across the team. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is precise communication especially critical for a nurse working across multiple specialties?

options.A: It guarantees that the patient will never require diagnostic imaging
options.B: It prevents duplication of services and mitigates medical errors
options.C: It allows the nurse to independently discharge patients from the hospital
options.D: It replaces the need for formal written patient medical records

explanation: Clear transfer of information across diverse departments protects patients from redundant procedures and communication mistakes. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: What two elements primarily constitute critical thinking in polyvalent nursing practice?

options.A: Delegation of all complex decision-making to senior administrators
options.B: Reliance exclusively on computerized diagnostic test results
options.C: Pattern recognition combined with rapid clinical reasoning
options.D: Blind obedience to rigid hospital operational guidelines

explanation: Critical thinking requires the nurse to recognize clinical patterns quickly and apply sound reasoning to patient situations. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: How does a polyvalent nurse manage patient care when advanced diagnostic technology is unavailable?

options.A: By relying on thorough physical assessment and logical deduction
options.B: By immediately discharging the patient until equipment is repaired
options.C: By pausing all nursing interventions until a specialist arrives
options.D: By guessing the diagnosis without performing any assessments

explanation: Resource constraints require strong clinical reasoning and robust physical assessment skills to guide safe care priorities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is a major structural challenge facing the Nigerian healthcare system that highlights the need for polyvalent nurses?

options.A: Excessive funding that complicates hospital operational budgeting
options.B: An overwhelming surplus of specialized intensive care physicians
options.C: Maldistribution of health personnel and infrastructural deficits
options.D: Complete elimination of rural healthcare clinics nationwide

explanation: Shortages and uneven distribution of specialized staff create a high demand for versatile generalist nurses in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)

question: A primary health center in a rural Nigerian community has only two nurses on duty to cover maternity, immunization, and emergency care. Which nursing model is most appropriate for this setting?

options.A: Polyvalent nursing, to handle multiple service areas flexibly
options.B: Strict hyper-specialization, where each nurse handles only one rare disease
options.C: Research-only nursing, pausing all direct patient care activities
options.D: Administrative nursing, focusing solely on office paper documentation

explanation: Skeletal staffing in rural health centers requires multi-skilled nurses who can safely manage diverse clinical demands. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)
